assumptions.assumption: one counter per switch rather than a shared sampling tick.
assumptions.reason: the request says noise is ignored however it lines up.
a switch being turned on is the usual event of interest.

behaviour: Each SW[k] is synchronised (two flops), then debounced on its own. The clean level L[k] changes only after the synchronised input has differed from it for DEBOUNCE_CYCLES consecutive clocks; a shorter difference restarts the count. No slow sampling tick - a difference shorter than DEBOUNCE_CYCLES never changes L[k], wherever it falls in time.
Because the levels reset to 0, a switch already up at reset gives a rising edge DEBOUNCE_CYCLES clocks after reset.
COUNT[k] (8 bits, wrapping at 256) adds 1 on every change of L[k], rising or falling, whatever the edge selection.

EDGES[k] is set on a rise of L[k] when RISE_EN[k] = 1, and on a fall when FALL_EN[k] = 1. It stays set until a shell write to EDGES with bit k = 1 (write-1-to-clear); if an edge and the clear fall on the same clock, the edge wins.

"""Acceptance tests of t1_debounce_bank against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from cocotb.triggers import ReadOnly, RisingEdge
from cocotb.utils import get_sim_time
from model import COUNT0, DESIGN_ID, EDGES, FALL_EN, LEVEL, RISE_EN, Model

NAMES = {LEVEL: "LEVEL", EDGES: "EDGES", RISE_EN: "RISE_EN", FALL_EN: "FALL_EN", 4: "COUNT0", 5: "COUNT1",
         6: "COUNT2", 7: "COUNT3"}


class Env:
    def __init__(self, dut) -> None:
        self.b = Board(dut, {"SW": 0})
        self.dut, self.m = dut, Model()
        self.n = self.b.param("DEBOUNCE_CYCLES")
        self.sw = 0

    async def start(self) -> None:
        await self.b.start()

    async def set_sw(self, v: int, settle: bool = True) -> None:
        self.sw = v & 0xFFFF
        self.dut.SW.value = self.sw
        if settle:
            await self.b.cycles(self.n + 8)
            self.m.settle(self.sw)

    async def wr(self, off: int, v: int) -> None:
        await self.b.write(off, v)
        self.m.write(off, v)

    async def check_regs(self) -> None:
        for off in range(8):
            await self.b.expect(off, self.m.read(off), NAMES[off])

    async def check_leds(self) -> None:
        led = await peek(self.b.clk, self.dut.LED)
        assert led == self.m.level, f"LED {led:04X} != model {self.m.level:04X}"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    assert await e.b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_glitch_on_slow_tick(dut):
    """Trap: the textbook debouncer samples each switch on a slow tick, so a short glitch that happens to cover a
    sampling instant changes the level. Glitches of 3 clocks are swept across every phase of a DEBOUNCE_CYCLES
    period (and longer ones up to DEBOUNCE_CYCLES - 1): none may change any level."""
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.set_sw(0x0F0F)
    await e.check_regs()
    base = e.sw
    for width, step in ((3, 3), (e.n - 1, 1), (e.n // 2, 5)):
        for _ in range(e.n // step + 2):
            dut.SW.value = base ^ 0xFFFF
            await e.b.cycles(width)
            dut.SW.value = base
            await e.b.cycles(e.n + step)
    await e.b.cycles(e.n + 8)
    await e.check_regs()                         # no level change, no count, no edge beyond the first settle
    await e.check_leds()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_levels_follow_switches(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for v in (0x0001, 0x8000, 0xFFFF, 0x0000, 0xA5C3, 0x5A3C):
        await e.set_sw(v)
        await e.check_leds()
        await e.b.expect(LEVEL, e.m.read(LEVEL), "LEVEL")
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_independent_timing(dut):
    """Each switch has its own debounce: a change on one never restarts or delays another."""
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    seen: dict[int, int] = {}

    async def watch():
        prev = 0
        while True:
            await RisingEdge(e.b.clk)
            await ReadOnly()
            v = int(dut.LED.value)
            for k in range(16):
                if (v ^ prev) >> k & 1 and k not in seen:
                    seen[k] = int(get_sim_time("ns")) // 10
            prev = v

    cocotb.start_soon(watch())
    t0 = int(get_sim_time("ns")) // 10
    dut.SW.value = 1 << 3                       # switch 3 up at t0
    await e.b.cycles(e.n // 2)
    dut.SW.value = 1 << 3 | 1 << 9              # switch 9 up half a debounce later
    for _ in range(3):                          # switch 12 chatters meanwhile
        await e.b.cycles(e.n // 6)
        dut.SW.value = int(dut.SW.value) | 1 << 12
        await e.b.cycles(2)
        dut.SW.value = int(dut.SW.value) & ~(1 << 12)
    await e.b.cycles(2 * e.n)
    assert set(seen) == {3, 9}, f"LEDs that changed: {sorted(seen)}"
    assert seen[9] - seen[3] == e.n // 2, f"switch 9 settled {seen[9] - seen[3]} clocks after 3, want {e.n // 2}"
    # v1.2: n + 1 .. n + 8 clocks (a two- to four-flop synchroniser plus one output register all pass)
    assert seen[3] - t0 - e.n in range(1, 9), f"switch 3 took {seen[3] - t0} clocks to settle"
    e.sw = 1 << 3 | 1 << 9
    e.m.settle(e.sw)
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_counts_and_clear(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for k, n in ((0, 3), (5, 2), (7, 5), (14, 1), (15, 4)):
        for _ in range(n):
            await e.set_sw(e.sw ^ 1 << k)
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(5, 0x1234)                       # clears counts 4..7 only
    await e.check_regs()
    for _ in range(258):                        # count 0 wraps at 256
        await e.set_sw(e.sw ^ 1)
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_edge_selection_and_w1c(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.wr(RISE_EN, 0x00FF)
    await e.wr(FALL_EN, 0x0F0F)
    await e.set_sw(0xFFFF)                      # rises: EDGES 0x00FF
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(EDGES, 0x000F)                   # W1C: clear four
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(EDGES, 0)                        # zeros clear nothing
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.set_sw(0x0000)                      # falls: adds 0x0F0F
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(EDGES, 0xFFFF)
    await e.wr(RISE_EN, 0)
    await e.wr(FALL_EN, 0)
    await e.set_sw(0xFFFF)                      # nothing selected: no flags, counts still move
    await e.set_sw(0x0000)
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_bounce_then_steady(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for w in (2, 7, 4, 11, 3):
        dut.SW.value = 0x0101
        await e.b.cycles(w)
        dut.SW.value = 0
        await e.b.cycles(w)
    await e.set_sw(0x0101)                      # one rise each, however much chatter before
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_register_rules(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.set_sw(0x00F0)
    await e.b.write(LEVEL, 0xFFFF)              # read-only
    await e.wr(RISE_EN, 0xABCD_1234)            # [15:0] only
    await e.wr(FALL_EN, 0x1_0000)
    await e.check_regs()
    for off in (0x08, 0x40, 0x7F):
        await e.b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_random_activity(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    rng = random.Random(int(cocotb.RANDOM_SEED))
    await e.wr(RISE_EN, rng.getrandbits(16))
    await e.wr(FALL_EN, rng.getrandbits(16))
    for _ in range(25):
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.15:
            mask = rng.getrandbits(16)
            dut.SW.value = e.sw ^ mask          # a glitch: shorter than the debounce time
            await e.b.cycles(rng.randrange(1, e.n))
            dut.SW.value = e.sw
            await e.b.cycles(e.n + 4)
        elif r < 0.25:
            await e.wr(rng.choice((EDGES, 4, 5, 6, 7)), rng.getrandbits(32))
        else:
            await e.set_sw(e.sw ^ rng.getrandbits(16))
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()

spec_md:
# Sixteen-switch debounce bank

I want all sixteen slide switches of the Nexys A7-100T cleaned up, each on its own.

- Every switch is synchronised and debounced separately: a switch's clean level only changes once the switch
  has stayed at the new level for the whole debounce time; anything shorter is noise and is ignored completely,
  however it lines up with anything else.
- LED[15:0] show the sixteen clean levels.
- For each switch, count how many times its clean level has changed (a small counter per switch is enough).
- Keep a register of sticky edge flags, one per switch, that I clear by writing ones to it. I want to choose, per
  switch, whether rising edges, falling edges or both set the flag.
- CPU_RESETN resets everything.
- Over the test shell (USB-UART, 115200 baud) I can read the clean levels, the counts and the edge flags, clear
  them, and set the edge selection. The design ID is "DBNK".

Test hooks: top module `t1_debounce_bank_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC, the test shell's
`CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters, plus `DEBOUNCE_CYCLES` (the debounce time in clocks)
as top-level parameters.
title: Sixteen-switch debounce bank

captions: Start: all clean levels 0, no edge flags, rising edges enabled, falling edges not.
Step 1: switches held at 0000000000000101 long enough; switches 0 and 2 change their clean level. New edge flags set: 0005.
Step 2: switches held at 0000000000000111 long enough; switch 1 changes its clean level. New edge flags set: 0002.
Step 3: writing ones with mask 0007 clears those edge flags, leaving 0000.
Step 4: falling edges are enabled for the switches in mask 0004.
Step 5: switches held at 0000000000000011 long enough; switch 2 changes its clean level. New edge flags set: 0004.
Step 6: switches held at 0000000000000111 long enough; switch 2 changes its clean level.
Step 7: switches held at 0000000000000100 long enough; switches 0 and 1 change their clean level.
Step 8: writing ones with mask 0004 clears those edge flags, leaving 0000.
Step 9: switches held at 1000000000000100 long enough; switch 15 changes its clean level. New edge flags set: 8000.
Step 10: switches held at 1000000000000000 long enough; switch 2 changes its clean level. New edge flags set: 0004.
Step 11: switches held at 1000000000000100 long enough; switch 2 changes its clean level.
Step 12: switches held at 0000000000000000 long enough; switches 2 and 15 change their clean level.
Step 13: writing ones with mask FFFF clears those edge flags, leaving 0000.
Step 14: switches held at 0000000000000001 long enough; switch 0 changes its clean level. New edge flags set: 0001.
trace.stimulus: Switch patterns are applied after each has been steady for longer than the debounce time (glitches shorter than that never reach the model). Between them the edge flags are cleared and falling edges are enabled for one switch.

what: A bank that cleans up every slide switch on the board separately. A switch's clean level only changes after it has held its new position for the whole debounce time, so shorter glitches are ignored however they line up. For each switch the design counts how many times the clean level changed, and keeps a sticky flag for rising and falling edges that the user can choose per switch and clear by writing ones.
where: Switch and button inputs on nearly every embedded product need this kind of conditioning, from front-panel keypads to limit switches on machines. Per-input edge flags and event counters are the usual way a processor is told that something changed.
